sections.title: Van and nincs
sections.content: To ask whether a dish is available, use *van* and *nincs* as you know them: *Van leves?* (Is there soup?) *Nincs desszert.* (There is no dessert.) The dish is not an object here, it is the thing that exists, so it has no *-t*. Compare *Kérek levest* (I ask for it, with *-t*) and *Van leves* (it exists, no *-t*).

sections.title: On the menu
sections.content: The menu is *az étlap*. In Hungarian things are "on" it: *étlap → étlapon*. So *Az étlapon van hal.* means "There is fish on the menu." To ask what is there, use *mi*: *Mi van az étlapon?*

sections.title: Asking and answering
rows: There is fish on the menu.

items.english: There is no fish, there is meat.

items.spanish: Az étlapon van leves és saláta.
items.english: There is soup and salad on the menu.

sections.content: After *van* and *nincs* the dish stays plain: *Nincs desszert*, not *Nincs desszertet*. Only a dish you ask for takes *-t*.
